# Adjudication Task — Chapter 719

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃719화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|퀘스트, [타락한 신물]을 수락하시겠습니까?
  6|
  7|Y / N
  8|
  9|
 10|
 11|갑작스럽게 눈앞에 떠오른 홀로그램 창은 이뿐만이 아니다.
 12|
 13|나는 새롭게 생성된 퀘스트 정보를 빠르게 눈으로 훑었다.
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|퀘스트
 18|
 19|
 20|
 21|[타락한 신물]
 22|
 23|
 24|
 25|한때 이 땅을 수호하던 신석(神石)은 이미 본래의 모습을 잃어버렸습니다.
 26|
 27|마기에 잠식당한 그것은 또 다른 재앙의 불씨와 같으며, 당신은 어떤 방식으로든 이 타락한 신물을 처분해야 합니다.
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|등급 : 초절정
 32|
 33|제한 : 진태경
 34|
 35|임무 : [타락한 신물] 처분 (미완료)
 36|
 37|보상 : 임무 수행 방식에 따라 변동
 38|
 39|실패 : [타락한 신물]의 마기 증가
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|
 44|
 45|퀘스트 정보창을 끝까지 읽은 나는 조용히 마음속으로 뇌까렸다.
 46|
 47|‘수락.’
 48|
 49|
 50|
 51|- 퀘스트, [타락한 신물]을 수락하셨습니다!
 52|
 53|
 54|
 55|지금까지 반강제로 진행되었던 몇몇 퀘스트와는 달리 이번에는 버젓이 선택지가 있었지만, 내게 있어 이건 거부할 수 없는 제안이나 마찬가지였다.
 56|
 57|‘언제까지 마기를 억누르고 있을 수만은 없어.’
 58|
 59|신석. 아니, 마기에 잠식당한 [타락한 신물]은 언제 터져도 이상하지 않을 폭탄이나 다름없다.
 60|
 61|그나마 갖고 있던 인물이 야수묘왕이라 다행이었지, 어지간한 절정 고수라 해도 저것에 담긴 마기를 감당할 수 없었을 것이다.
 62|
 63|‘퀘스트 정보창에 적혀 있는 내용처럼, 어떻게든 처리해야 한다.’
 64|
 65|균열을 닫기까지 얼마나 많은 희생을 치러야 했던가.
 66|
 67|마지막 순간 스스로 몸을 내던졌던 수호령을 생각해서라도 저 폭탄이 터지는 것만큼은 막아야 했다.
 68|
 69|그리고 지금 이 순간, 이와 같은 생각을 떠올린 것은 나 혼자만이 아니었다.
 70|
 71|“이 정도의 마기라니, 안 되겠군.”
 72|
 73|눈살을 찌푸린 채 중얼거린 적천강이 나와 야수묘왕을 향해 손짓했다.
 74|
 75|“빠져 있어라. 노부가 처리할 테니.”
 76|
 77|적천강이 한 말의 의미를 짐작한 듯, 야수묘왕의 눈동자가 크게 뜨였다.
 78|
 79|“적 노, 그 말씀은 설마.”
 80|
 81|“네놈이 생각하는 그 설마가 맞다. 화근이 될 가능성이 있다면 아예 싹을 뽑아 버려야지.”
 82|
 83|“하지만 이건…… 결코 쉽게 파괴할 수 있는 성질의 것이 아닙니다.”
 84|
 85|그리고 우려를 표하는 야수묘왕에게 돌아온 적천강의 대답은, 실로 짧고 간결했다.
 86|
 87|“그건 네놈이나 그렇고.”
 88|
 89|“…….”
 90|
 91|“난 돼.”
 92|
 93|그야말로 씹상남자식 화법.
 94|
 95|짤막한 한마디로 남만 최고의 짐승남인 야수묘왕마저 입 닥치게 만든 적천강이 천천히 손을 뻗었다.
 96|
 97|화아악.
 98|
 99|그의 손을 타고 모여들기 시작한 열양지기가 끔찍한 열기를 토해 낸다. 사방에서 피어오르는 아지랑이에 흡사 공간이 일그러지는 듯한 착각마저 들 정도다.
100|
101|하지만…….
102|
103|“노야.”
104|
105|고심 끝에 불쑥 튀어나온 한 마디.
106|
107|막 출수(出手)하려던 적천강이 문득 움직임을 멈췄다.
108|
109|“뭐냐?”
110|
111|“안 하는 게 좋을 것 같은데요. 그거.”
112|
113|“왜?”
114|
115|“나름대로 좀 생각해 봤는데, 함부로 건드리면 재미없을 것 같아서요.”
116|
117|“뭐라?”
118|
119|내 진중한 목소리에, 적천강이 눈을 크게 떴다.
120|
121|“아니, 네놈이 생각이란 걸 했단 말이냐?”
122|
123|“…….”
124|
125|말문이 턱 막히네, 아주.
126|
127|짜게 식은 내 표정을 바라보며 헛기침한 적천강이 입을 열었다.
128|
129|“이대로 두면 언제고 화근이 된다. 한시라도 빠르게 처리하는 것이 맞아.”
130|
131|“그건 저도 알죠.”
132|
133|“아는 놈이 왜 그러느냐? 노부가 못 미더워서?”
134|
135|“어허. 말씀을 왜 그렇게 하세요. 제가 노야 아니면 누구를 믿는다고.”
136|
137|대답은 이렇게 했지만, 사실 절반 정도는 그런 마음이 없지 않아 있다.
138|
139|좀 더 정확히 말하자면, 적천강이 못 미더워서가 아니라 혹시나 하는 우려 때문이다.
140|
141|‘만약에 완전히 파괴하지 못한다면?’
142|
143|지금의 [타락한 신물]은…… 예를 들자면 내 앞에 놓여 있는 찻잔 같은 거다.
144|
145|잔이 온전하다면 찻물은 흘러넘치지 않는다. 그러나 찻잔이 깨지면, 찻물은 사방으로 넘쳐 흐를 것이다.
146|
147|‘마기를 억누르지 못하게 되면, 그땐 또 한 번 지랄 나는 거고.’
148|
149|미친 호랑이 한 마리가 아무리 날뛰어 봤자 때려잡으면 그만이다. 하지만 마기가 퍼져 나간다면 골치가 아파진다.
150|
151|아니, 그때는 골치 아픈 정도로 끝나면 다행이겠지.
152|
153|그래서 적천강을 말려야 했다.
154|
155|내가 얼마나 그를 신뢰하느냐와는 관계없이, 이런 도박에 다른 사람의 목숨을 판돈으로 밀어 넣을 수는 없으니까.
156|
157|‘그게 천분의 일. 만분의 일밖에 되지 않는 확률이라 해도 지금은 안 돼.’
158|
159|이미 너무 많은 피를 흘렸다.
160|
161|장렬히 싸우다 죽고, 이지를 상실한 괴물이 되어 죽고, 칼 한 번 잡아본 적 없는 이들조차 그 지옥도를 탈출하는 과정에서 적지 않게 죽어 나갔다.
162|
163|아마 수호령이 스스로를 희생하여 균열을 닫지 않았다면, 지금쯤 피해는 눈덩이처럼 불어났을…… 잠깐.
164|
165|‘수호령?’
166|
167|문득 떠오른 기시감과 함께 그 세 글자가 뇌리에서 빙글빙글 맴돈다.
168|
169|녀석을 처음 만난 날부터 지금까지의 기억들이 차례차례 눈과 귀를 스치고, 마침내 한 줄기 깨달음을 향해 달려 나갔다.
170|
171|그리고 어느 순간.
172|
173|“아.”
174|
175|나도 모르게 입술을 비집고 흘러나온 외마디 탄성.
176|
177|이놈이 갑자기 왜 이러나, 하는 표정으로 나를 바라보던 적천강과 야수묘왕이 차례대로 입을 열었다.
178|
179|“그래, 갑자기 왜 또 혼자서 지랄 염병이냐? 노부도 좀 알자.”
180|
181|“무슨 묘책(妙策)이라도 떠오른 게 아니겠습니까?”
182|
183|글쎄. 이걸 묘책이라고 부를 정도인지는 모르겠다.
184|
185|적어도 아직까지는.
186|
187|하지만 지금 내가 품고 있는 짐작이 사실이라면…… 충분히 시도해 볼 만하다.
188|
189|‘적어도 손해 볼 건 없겠지.’
190|
191|내심 중얼거린 나는, 아직 닫지 않은 퀘스트 창과 대답을 기다리고 있는 두 사람의 얼굴을 차례대로 바라보았다. 그리고 어깨를 으쓱하며 입을 열었다.
192|
193|“두 분 모두, 잠깐 저랑 같이 바람 좀 쐬시죠.”
194|
195|
196|
197|* * *
198|
199|
200|
201|두두두두!
202|
203|일제히 바람을 가르며 달려나가는 일단의 무리는 조촐했다. 아니, 머릿수만 보면 ‘무리’라는 단어 자체부터 어불성설일지도 모른다.
204|
205|호랑이 셋에 사람 셋.
206|
207|하지만 가까이에서 그 면면을 살피면 이야기는 달라진다. 당장 내 양옆으로 달려 나가는 두 사람만 해도 그렇다.
208|
209|“짐승이 빨라 봤자 얼마나 빠를까 싶었는데, 이것도 썩 나쁘진 않구먼. 안장도 편안하고.”
210|
211|흥미로운 눈빛으로 열심히 달려나가는 호랑이를 요모조모 뜯어보는 적천강의 모습에, 왼편에서 달려 나가던 야수묘왕이 넙죽 대답했다.
212|
213|“저희 남만야수궁에서도 가장 용맹하고 빠른 녀석 중 하납니다. 정마대전 당시에 저와 함께 참전한 녀석의 후손이기도 하지요.”
214|
215|“오호. 그 막사 앞에 웅크려 앉아있던 커다란 놈? 기억나는군. 왠지 낯이 익다 싶었지.”
216|
217|그래. 좌청룡 우백호가 별거냐.
218|
219|좌화왕 우묘왕이라는 이 미친 라인업에 가슴이 절로 웅장해진다.
220|
221|설령 남천마후가 살아 돌아와도 발라 먹을 수 있는 무시무시한 전력.
222|
223|국밥보다 더한 든든함을 느끼는 내 귓가로 이어진 두 사람의 대화가 두런두런 들려왔다.
224|
225|“이놈 보면 볼수록 괜찮은데. 체력 좋고. 발도 빠른 데다 딱 봐도 영특해 보이고.”
226|
227|야수묘왕이 흐뭇하게 웃었다.
228|
229|“제가 특별히 공들여 키웠지요. 새끼 시절에는 워낙 입이 짧아 고생했는데, 그럴 때마다 제가 손수 젖까지 먹여 가며 키운 녀석입니다.”
230|
231|“뭣이? 네놈이 직접?”
232|
233|“……말이 그렇다는 거지. 지금 적 노께서 생각하시는 그런 건 아닙니다.”
234|
235|야수묘왕의 우람한 대흉근을 유심히 살피던 적천강이 고개를 끄덕였다.
236|
237|“뭐, 그렇다 치지.”
238|
239|“아니, 그렇게 말씀하시면 뭔가 이상…….”
240|
241|“여하튼 됐다. 이놈은 노부가 데려가는 것으로 하지.”
242|
243|그 순간, 야수묘왕의 입가에 맺혀 있던 미소가 사라졌다.
244|
245|“예?”
246|
247|“뭘 되물어? 그럼 중원까지 돌아가는 길에도 뭐 빠지게 뛰게 할 생각이었느냐?”
248|
249|“그, 그건 당연히 아닙니다만, 지금 타고 계신 녀석은 후배가 늘그막에 자식처럼 기른 놈이라…….”
250|
251|“줘.”
252|
253|“아니 그.”
254|
255|“해 줘.”
256|
257|“…….”
258|
259|“정 싫으면 저 녀석을 데려가지. 딱 봐도 영물 같은데.”
260|
261|적천강이 지목한 ‘저 녀석’을 바라본 야수묘왕이 황급히 고개를 내저었다.
262|
263|“헉. 저 녀석만큼은 안 됩니다. 애당초 잠시 빌려온 거고요.”
264|
265|“노부가 된다면?”
266|
267|“제, 제가 직접 기른 것도 아니고, 아비가 되어 자식놈이 형제처럼 생각하는 놈을 어떻게 보내겠습니까.”
268|
269|“오늘따라 하늘이 맑구나. 혓바닥은 길고.”
270|
271|잠시 침묵하던 야수묘왕이 침울한 목소리로 대답했다.
272|
273|“……알겠습니다. 지금 타고 계신 녀석을 내어 드리지요.”
274|
275|“그렇게 권하니 어쩔 수 없지. 네 호의를 받아들이마.”
276|
277|“…….”
278|
279|웅장하긴 개뿔이.
280|
281|그 노망났던 화왕이 맞나. 화왕은 진짜 전설이다…….
282|
283|그리고 내가 조촐해진 가슴을 애써 가다듬고 있을 때, 나를 태우고 열심히 달려가던 ‘저 녀석’이 낮은 울음소리를 흘렸다.
284|
285|크르릉.
286|
287|슬쩍 눈까지 마주치는 모습을 보아하니, 저놈도 자신이 지금 막 화왕이라는 개장수 손아귀에서 간신히 벗어났다는 걸 아는 모양이다.
288|
289|불쌍한 마음이 든 나는 파르르 떨리는 새하얀 털을 부드럽게 쓸어 주었다.
290|
291|“괜찮아, 인마. 넌 살아남았어.”
292|
293|끼이잉.
294|
295|어미 잃은 강아지처럼 처연한 울음소리를 흘린 무야호가 슬그머니 걸음을 늦추었다.
296|
297|적천강 앞에서 뛰어난 모습을 보여 봤자 중원 땅까지 끌려갈 확률만 높아진다는 걸 본능적으로 깨달은 것이 분명했다.
298|
299|다행히도, 적천강의 관심은 다른 곳으로 옮겨 간 직후였다.
300|
301|“저건……?”
302|
303|서서히 흐려지는 말꼬리.
304|
305|적천강이 바라보는 방향의 끝에는, 완전히 전소(全燒)되다시피 한 민둥산이 있었다.
306|
307|아니, 저 볼품없는 민둥산에도 이름은 있다.
308|
309|애뇌산(哀牢山)이라는, 이 땅에서 살아가는 이들이라면 모를 수 없는 이름이.
310|
311|그리고 내가 막 그에 관하여 설명하려던 그 순간, 적천강이 눈을 부릅뜨며 외쳤다.
312|
313|“감히 어떤 호로 개잡놈의 새끼가 소중한 산천초목을 태워 먹었단 말이냐!”
314|
315|“…….”
316|

I looked from the still-open Quest window to the two men waiting for an answer, then shrugged.

[P68]
“Why don’t you both come get some air with me?”

[P69]
* * *

[P70]
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*

[P71]
Our little group raced through the wind. With only three tigers and three people, *group* might have been too grand a word.

[P72]
Then again, it depended on who those people were. The two riding on either side of me made all the difference.

[P73]
“I wondered how fast a beast could be, but this isn’t bad. Comfortable saddle, too.”

[P74]
Jeok Cheongang inspected the tiger running beneath him with interest. The Beast Miao King, riding to my left, answered at once.

[P75]
“He’s one of the bravest and fastest tigers in the Nanman Beast Palace. He’s descended from the one that fought alongside me in the Great Faction War.”

[P76]
“Oh? That big fellow who used to crouch outside your barracks? I remember him. Thought this one looked familiar.”

[P77]
Yeah. Who needed an Azure Dragon on the left and a White Tiger on the right?

[P78]
I had the Fire King on my left and the Miao King on my right. My chest swelled at the thought of that insane lineup. If the Southern Heaven Demon Empress came back to life, these two could take her apart.

[P79]
I felt safer than I would with a bowl of gukbap in front of me.[^1] Their conversation continued beside me.

[P80]
“The more I look at him, the more I like him. Good stamina, quick feet. Looks clever, too.”

[P81]
The Beast Miao King smiled with pride.

[P82]
“I took special care raising him. He was such a picky eater as a cub that I had to feed him milk myself.”

[P83]
“What? *You* fed him?”

[P84]
“……It’s a figure of speech. Not what you’re thinking, Old Master Jeok.”

[P85]
Jeok Cheongang studied the Beast Miao King’s massive chest, then nodded.

[P86]
“If you say so.”

[P87]
“No, when you say it like that, it sounds as though—”

[P88]
“Never mind. I’ll take this one with me.”

[P89]
The smile vanished from the Beast Miao King’s face.

[P90]
“Pardon?”

[P91]
“Why ask? Were you planning to make me run my legs off all the way back to the Central Plains?”

[P92]
“O-of course not. But I raised the one you’re riding like a son in my old age…”

[P93]
“Give him to me.”

[P94]
“But—”

[P95]
“Go on.”

[P96]
“……”

[P97]
“If you don’t want to, I’ll take that one instead. He looks like a spiritual creature.”

[P98]
The Beast Miao King looked at the tiger Jeok Cheongang had pointed out and shook his head in alarm.

[P99]
“Oh! Anyone but him. I’ve only borrowed him for a little while.”

[P100]
“What if I say I’m taking him?”

[P101]
“I-I didn’t raise him myself. And how could I, as a father, give away someone my son thinks of as a brother?”

[P102]
“The sky’s clear today. Your tongue’s awfully long.”

[P103]
After a moment’s silence, the Beast Miao King answered glumly.

[P104]
“……Understood. You may have the one you’re riding.”

[P105]
“Well, if you insist. I’ll accept your generosity.”

[P106]
“……”

[P107]
So much for my chest swelling with pride.

[P108]
Was this really the senile Fire King I knew? The Fire King truly was a legend…

[P109]
As I tried to recover from the spectacle, the tiger carrying me gave a low growl.

[P110]
*Grrr.*

[P111]
He glanced back at me. He seemed to know he’d narrowly escaped the clutches of the Fire King, that dog trader. I felt sorry for him and gently stroked his trembling white fur.

[P112]
“It’s okay, buddy. You survived.”

[P113]
*Whine.*

[P114]
Muyaho let out a forlorn little cry, like a puppy that had lost its mother, and slowed down. He must have realized that showing off in front of Jeok Cheongang would only make it more likely he’d be dragged all the way to the Central Plains.

[P115]
Fortunately, Jeok Cheongang’s attention had already shifted.

[P116]
“What’s that…?”

[P117]
His voice trailed off. Ahead of us stood a bare mountain, almost completely burned.

[P118]
No, even that sorry-looking mountain had a name: Ailao Mountain. Everyone who lived in this land knew it.

[P119]
I was about to explain when Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flew wide.

[P120]
“What goddamn son of a bitch burned all those precious trees and plants?”

[P121]
“……”

[P122]
“……”

[P123]
For an instant, the Beast Miao King and I exchanged a heated glance. Then I answered with all the outrage I could muster.

[P124]
“Dark Heaven.”

[P125]
Some truths are better left unknown.

[P126]
* * *

[P127]
Once Jeok Cheongang realized the sorry-looking mountain was our destination, he frowned.

[P128]
“Did we come all this way to plant trees?”

[P129]
“……I’m asking because I genuinely want to know. Just how crazy do you think I am?”

[P130]
What a ridiculous question.

[P131]
It wasn’t Arbor Day. Even if it had been, I wouldn’t be planting trees. I’d brought them to what remained of Ailao Mountain for a reason.

[P132]
“This way.”

[P133]
The Beast Miao King soon realized where I was going.

[P134]
“The Poisonblood Grounds. Or should I call it the Sacred Land now?”

[P135]
It would have been stranger if he *hadn’t* known. Yohi must have told him roughly what had happened, even if she’d left out the details.

[P136]
I shook my head.

[P137]
“They’re different. The Poisonblood Grounds are the Poisonblood Grounds. The Sacred Land is the Sacred Land.”

[P138]
The two places were separate. The Poisonblood Grounds were a land of death made by human hands. The Sacred Land was Nanman’s heart—a land of life.

[P139]
*Life itself.*

[P140]
I set the Corrupted Divine Artifact on the ground. Demonic qi drifted from it like mist, and Muyaho growled softly.

[P141]
But though darkness had consumed it, its essence had not changed.

[P142]
*Shhhhhh.*

[P143]
The ground pulsed like a beating heart. A veil lifted from another world that had been hidden for countless ages.

[P144]
Then I saw it: a space filled with warm radiance, and at its center, a small pond shining more brilliantly than anything else.

[P145]
“Ah.”

[P146]
“That’s…”

[P147]
Jeok Cheongang’s and the Beast Miao King’s exclamations faded without either man finishing his thought.

[P148]
But I knew what they had felt. And I knew what I had to do.

[P149]
*Purification.*

[P150]
Today, a new sacred stone would be born.

[P151]
[^1]: Gukbap is rice served in hot soup, a common comfort food in Korea.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

> Will you accept?
>
> **Y / N**

[P3]
That wasn’t the only holographic window to appear before me. I quickly scanned the information for the new Quest.

[P4]
> **System**
>
> **Quest**
>
> **Corrupted Divine Artifact**
>
> The sacred stone that once protected this land has lost its original form.
>
> Consumed by demonic qi, it is a spark that could ignite another calamity. You must dispose of this Corrupted Divine Artifact by any means.
>
> **Grade:** Supreme Peak
>
> **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung
>
> **Mission:** Dispose of Corrupted Divine Artifact (Incomplete)
>
> **Reward:** Varies according to how the mission is carried out
>
> **Failure:** Increase in the Corrupted Divine Artifact’s demonic qi

[P5]
I read to the end, then answered silently.

[P6]
*Accept.*

[P7]
> **System**
>
> You have accepted the Quest **Corrupted Divine Artifact**!

[P8]
Unlike some of the Quests I’d been more or less forced into, this one gave me a choice. But as far as I was concerned, refusing wasn’t an option.

[P9]
*We can’t keep suppressing the demonic qi forever.*

[P10]
The sacred stone—no, the Corrupted Divine Artifact—was a bomb that could go off at any moment. We were lucky the Beast Miao King had been keeping it. An ordinary Peak master couldn’t have withstood the demonic qi inside it.

[P11]
*Like the Quest says, we have to deal with it somehow.*

[P12]
How many people had we lost closing the rift? For the sake of the guardian spirit that had thrown itself into it at the very end, I couldn’t let that bomb go off.

[P13]
I wasn’t the only one who thought so.

[P14]
“This much demonic qi… No.”

[P15]
Jeok Cheongang frowned and waved the Beast Miao King and me back.

[P16]
“Stand aside. This old man will handle it.”

[P17]
The Beast Miao King’s eyes widened as he realized what Jeok Cheongang meant.

[P18]
“Old Master Jeok, surely you don’t mean…”

[P19]
“Exactly what you think. If it might cause trouble, we pull it out by the roots.”

[P20]
“But this… won’t be easy to destroy.”

[P21]
Jeok Cheongang’s answer was short.

[P22]
“For you, maybe.”

[P23]
“……”

[P24]
“I can do it.”

[P25]
That was some fucking macho-man talk.

[P26]
One sentence had silenced even the Beast Miao King, the beastliest man in Nanman. Jeok Cheongang slowly reached out.

[P27]
*Whoosh.*

[P28]
Scorching Yang Qi gathered around his hand, giving off such terrible heat that the haze rising on every side made the air seem to warp.

[P29]
But—

[P30]
“Old Master.”

[P31]
The words slipped out after a moment’s thought. Jeok Cheongang stopped just as he was about to strike.

[P32]
“What?”

[P33]
“I don’t think you should do that.”

[P34]
“Why?”

[P35]
“I’ve been thinking. If we break it without knowing what’ll happen, things could get ugly.”

[P36]
“What?”

[P37]
His eyes widened at my serious tone.

[P38]
“You mean you actually thought?”

[P39]
“……”

[P40]
He had me there. Not in the way he meant, but I couldn’t think of a word to say.

[P41]
Jeok Cheongang saw my expression, cleared his throat, and went on. “If we leave it alone, it’ll cause trouble sooner or later. We should deal with it as soon as possible.”

[P42]
“I know.”

[P43]
“Then why stop me? Don’t you trust this old man?”

[P44]
“Oh, come on. Why would you say that? If I can’t trust you, Old Master, who can I trust?”

[P45]
That was my answer. In truth, about half of me did have doubts.

[P46]
Not because I distrusted Jeok Cheongang. I was worried about what might happen.

[P47]
*What if he doesn’t destroy it completely?*

[P48]
The Corrupted Divine Artifact was like the teacup in front of me. While the cup stayed intact, the tea stayed inside. Break the cup, and it would spill everywhere.

[P49]
*If we lose control of the demonic qi, we’ll have another goddamn disaster on our hands.*

[P50]
One mad tiger, however wildly it rampaged, could be beaten down. Demonic qi spreading through the area was another matter. If that happened, we’d be lucky if it was merely *troublesome*.

[P51]
I had to stop Jeok Cheongang. No matter how much I trusted him, I couldn’t stake other people’s lives on this gamble.

[P52]
*Even if the chance is one in a thousand—or one in ten thousand—not now.*

[P53]
Too much blood had been spilled already.

[P54]
People had died fighting to the bitter end. Others had lost their minds, become monsters, and died that way. Even people who had never held a sword had died in considerable numbers trying to escape that hellscape.

[P55]
If the guardian spirit hadn’t sacrificed itself to close the rift, the casualties would be mounting even now…

[P56]
Wait.

[P57]
*The guardian spirit?*

[P58]
A sudden sense of déjà vu came over me. Those words circled in my mind as memories from the day I first met it flashed past, one after another, drawing me toward a single realization.

[P59]
And then—

[P60]
“Ah.”

[P61]
The sound escaped before I knew it.

[P62]
Jeok Cheongang and the Beast Miao King stared at me as if wondering what the hell was wrong with me. Jeok Cheongang spoke first.

[P63]
“Why the fuck are you carrying on by yourself now? Let this old man in on it.”

[P64]
“Have you thought of a way?” the Beast Miao King asked.

[P65]
Maybe. I didn’t know whether it deserved to be called a plan. Not yet. But if I was right, it was worth trying.

[P66]
*At least we won’t lose anything.*

[P67]
I looked from the still-open Quest window to the two men waiting for an answer, then shrugged.

[P68]
“Why don’t you both come get some air with me?”

[P69]
* * *

[P70]
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*

[P71]
Our little group raced through the wind. With only three tigers and three people, *group* might have been too grand a word.

[P72]
Then again, it depended on who those people were. The two riding on either side of me made all the difference.

[P73]
“I wondered how fast a beast could be, but this isn’t bad. Comfortable saddle, too.”

[P74]
Jeok Cheongang inspected the tiger running beneath him with interest. The Beast Miao King, riding to my left, answered at once.

[P75]
“He’s one of the bravest and fastest tigers in the Nanman Beast Palace. He’s descended from the one that fought alongside me in the Great Faction War.”

[P76]
“Oh? That big fellow who used to crouch outside your barracks? I remember him. Thought this one looked familiar.”

[P77]
Yeah. Who needed an Azure Dragon on the left and a White Tiger on the right?

[P78]
I had the Fire King on my left and the Miao King on my right. My chest swelled at the thought of that insane lineup. If the Southern Heaven Demon Empress came back to life, these two could take her apart.

[P79]
I felt safer than I would with a bowl of gukbap in front of me.[^1] Their conversation continued beside me.

[P80]
“The more I look at him, the more I like him. Good stamina, quick feet. Looks clever, too.”

[P81]
The Beast Miao King smiled with pride.

[P82]
“I took special care raising him. He was such a picky eater as a cub that I had to feed him milk myself.”

[P83]
“What? *You* fed him?”

[P84]
“……It’s a figure of speech. Not what you’re thinking, Old Master Jeok.”

[P85]
Jeok Cheongang studied the Beast Miao King’s massive chest, then nodded.

[P86]
“If you say so.”

[P87]
“No, when you say it like that, it sounds as though—”

[P88]
“Never mind. I’ll take this one with me.”

[P89]
The smile vanished from the Beast Miao King’s face.

[P90]
“Pardon?”

[P91]
“Why ask? Were you planning to make me run my legs off all the way back to the Central Plains?”

[P92]
“O-of course not. But I raised the one you’re riding like a son in my old age…”

[P93]
“Give him to me.”

[P94]
“But—”

[P95]
“Go on.”

[P96]
“……”

[P97]
“If you don’t want to, I’ll take that one instead. He looks like a spiritual creature.”

[P98]
The Beast Miao King looked at the tiger Jeok Cheongang had pointed out and shook his head in alarm.

[P99]
“Oh! Anyone but him. I’ve only borrowed him for a little while.”

[P100]
“What if I say I’m taking him?”

[P101]
“I-I didn’t raise him myself. And how could I, as a father, give away someone my son thinks of as a brother?”

[P102]
“The sky’s clear today. Your tongue’s awfully long.”

[P103]
After a moment’s silence, the Beast Miao King answered glumly.

[P104]
“……Understood. You may have the one you’re riding.”

[P105]
“Well, if you insist. I’ll accept your generosity.”

[P106]
“……”

[P107]
So much for my chest swelling with pride.

[P108]
Was this really the senile Fire King I knew? The Fire King truly was a legend…

[P109]
As I tried to recover from the spectacle, the tiger carrying me gave a low growl.

[P110]
*Grrr.*

[P111]
He glanced back at me. He seemed to know he’d narrowly escaped the clutches of the Fire King, that dog trader. I felt sorry for him and gently stroked his trembling white fur.

[P112]
“It’s okay, buddy. You survived.”

[P113]
*Whine.*

[P114]
Muyaho let out a forlorn little cry, like a puppy that had lost its mother, and slowed down. He must have realized that showing off in front of Jeok Cheongang would only make it more likely he’d be dragged all the way to the Central Plains.

[P115]
Fortunately, Jeok Cheongang’s attention had already shifted.

[P116]
“What’s that…?”

[P117]
His voice trailed off. Ahead of us stood a bare mountain, almost completely burned.

[P118]
No, even that sorry-looking mountain had a name: Ailao Mountain. Everyone who lived in this land knew it.

[P119]
I was about to explain when Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flew wide.

[P120]
“What goddamn son of a bitch burned all those precious trees and plants?”

[P121]
“……”

[P122]
“……”

[P123]
For an instant, the Beast Miao King and I exchanged a heated glance. Then I answered with all the outrage I could muster.

[P124]
“Dark Heaven.”

[P125]
Some truths are better left unknown.

[P126]
* * *

[P127]
Once Jeok Cheongang realized the sorry-looking mountain was our destination, he frowned.

[P128]
“Did we come all this way to plant trees?”

[P129]
“……I’m asking because I genuinely want to know. Just how crazy do you think I am?”

[P130]
What a ridiculous question.

[P131]
It wasn’t Arbor Day. Even if it had been, I wouldn’t be planting trees. I’d brought them to what remained of Ailao Mountain for a reason.

[P132]
“This way.”

[P133]
The Beast Miao King soon realized where I was going.

[P134]
“The Poisonblood Grounds. Or should I call it the Sacred Land now?”

[P135]
It would have been stranger if he *hadn’t* known. Yohi must have told him roughly what had happened, even if she’d left out the details.

[P136]
I shook my head.

[P137]
“They’re different. The Poisonblood Grounds are the Poisonblood Grounds. The Sacred Land is the Sacred Land.”

[P138]
The two places were separate. The Poisonblood Grounds were a land of death made by human hands. The Sacred Land was Nanman’s heart—a land of life.

[P139]
*Life itself.*

[P140]
I set the Corrupted Divine Artifact on the ground. Demonic qi drifted from it like mist, and Muyaho growled softly.

[P141]
But though darkness had consumed it, its essence had not changed.

[P142]
*Shhhhhh.*

[P143]
The ground pulsed like a beating heart. A veil lifted from another world that had been hidden for countless ages.

[P144]
Then I saw it: a space filled with warm radiance, and at its center, a small pond shining more brilliantly than anything else.

[P145]
“Ah.”

[P146]
“That’s…”

[P147]
Jeok Cheongang’s and the Beast Miao King’s exclamations faded without either man finishing his thought.

[P148]
But I knew what they had felt. And I knew what I had to do.

[P149]
*Purification.*

[P150]
Today, a new sacred stone would be born.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
